biomarkers.name: 1p/19q whole-arm codeletion
biomarkers.clinical_use: Defining feature. Predicts favorable response to RT plus PCV chemotherapy; associated with best prognosis among diffuse gliomas

biomarkers.name: IDH1 R132 / IDH2 R172
biomarkers.clinical_use: Combined with 1p/19q codeletion defines the entity

biomarkers.name: TERT promoter mutations
biomarkers.clinical_use: Very common; supports diagnosis in the appropriate molecular context

biomarkers.name: CIC, FUBP1
biomarkers.clinical_use: Common accompanying alterations — supports oligodendroglioma classification

biomarkers.name: MGMT promoter methylation
biomarkers.clinical_use: Common in IDH-mutant gliomas; prognostic and may be associated with alkylator sensitivity, but predictive value specifically in oligodendroglioma is less clearly established than in glioblastoma

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Round nuclei with perinuclear halos ('fried egg' appearance in permanent sections), delicate 'chicken-wire' branching vasculature, microcalcifications
histomorphological_subtype.grading: WHO grade 2 or 3 based on cellularity, mitoses, microvascular proliferation, necrosis

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Cold — like other diffuse gliomas; microglia/macrophage predominant infiltrate
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Delicate 'chicken-wire' capillary network; frequent microcalcifications; infiltrative growth along cortex

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) — supported by developmental and transcriptional studies, though exact cell of origin remains not definitively proven in humans
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Neuroectoderm — OPCs migrate throughout brain during development from subventricular germinal zones
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Oligodendrocytic differentiation (OLIG2+, S100+, GFAP focal) with characteristic 'fried egg' cells (retracted cytoplasm artifact) and 'chicken-wire' vasculature
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Combined IDH mutation + 1p/19q co-deletion defines the entity; CIC (chromosome 19) and FUBP1 (chromosome 1) mutations are common accompanying alterations related to the codeleted chromosomal arms; TERT promoter mutations are frequent and contribute to telomere maintenance
